subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi John / Priya

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're all aligned and to capture next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Primary pain: inconsistent latency for customer-facing AI features and high per-token cost during peak querying.
- Secondary: current system has limited support for streaming responses and function-calling integrations, making conversational tool invocation brittle.
- Goal: reduce median response latency to <350ms for 2k RPS during typical peak windows, and cut per-token inference cost by ~30% through batching, caching, and quantization.

What we discussed (technical fit)
- SDK changes: minimal
Redwood's SDK supports a drop-in client; we'll provide a small adapter if your call signature differs. We discussed an SDK patch to add structured-output validation (JSON schema enforcement) and optional streaming hooks for partial UI updates.
- Function calling: Redwood supports function/tool calls; we recommend modeling low-latency tool invocations as lightweight function calls (stateless) and heavier invocations via async hooks.
- Streaming: streaming tokens for the UI is supported; we'll demonstrate on the PoC how to wire partial token streaming + reconnect semantics.
- Structured outputs / JSON schema: we can enforce a schema at the runtime to avoid post-processing parsing errors.
- Embeddings & reranking: we suggested using a hybrid approach
precompute embeddings for candidate docs, use lightweight dot-product scoring at query time, then rerank top-K with the LLM for final output quality.

Proposed PoC scope and success criteria
- 4-week PoC: integrate Redwood SDK into one service path (search-to-response flow).
- Deliverables: working integration with streaming UI, function-calling demo, structured output validation, embedding-based reranker with baseline vs Redwood measurement.
- Success metrics: latency <350ms median on target load, reranking improved NDCG by >=8% over current baseline, per-token cost savings >=25% at 95th percentile.

Risks / open questions
- SOC2 evidence and deployment model for private data. (John, you flagged compliance as a gating item.)
- Network topology for PoC if you prefer VPC peering for Dedicated vs Hosted run.
- Sizing and expected token counts for peak windows (we asked for sample telemetry).

Next steps
1) Marissa to share technical summary and proposed SOW + PoC timeline (attached).
2) Acme to share: sample telemetry (qps, token distribution), security questionnaire, and preferred billing/contact.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical kickoff week of Mar 8 — suggest Tue/Wed morning PST.

Attachments: redwood-technical-summary.pdf (high-level technical fit and PoC plan)

Thanks
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0138

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 18:02:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifying Qs before we loop security and schedule kickoff:

1) SDK / API compatibility: Our service currently calls a custom client that expects a streaming gRPC response with a continuous events stream. How invasive is the SDK adapter? Do you support gRPC streaming out of the box or would we run a small proxy?

2) Latency SLA: The <350ms median target is ambitious — how do you plan to account for cold KV cache misses and initial model load? Can you share any benchmarks for similar configuration?

3) SOC2 / compliance: We need SOC2 Type II evidence and an outline for VPC/private deployment options. Is Redwood's Private deployment an option during PoC, or is that only for production?

4) Cost model: For the PoC, can we get a capped spend or evaluation credits? We need to ensure this fits the procurement window.

Also looping Priya because she's owning procurement/compliance on our side.
—John

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

John, thanks for the great questions. Answers below and I've looped Michael (Solutions Engineer) and Dev (Platform PM) to own the technical follow-ups.

1) SDK / gRPC streaming
- Redwood SDK: the default SDK uses HTTP/2 streaming for partial responses; we also support gRPC streaming in our private/dedicated runtime. For hosted PoC we typically run a tiny adapter proxy (2-3 files) that translates your gRPC stream to Redwood's streaming HTTP/2 events. Michael can share a sample adapter repo.

2) Latency SLA and cold starts
- Approach: we provision warmed pools for the PoC path and use continuous batching + KV prefix caching to mitigate cold-hit cost. Cold model loads are accounted for in the first-hour ramp; our PoC SLO target uses warmed instances. Michael: attaching short benchmark summary we've used with similar SaaS search workloads.

3) SOC2 / Private deployment during PoC
- SOC2: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant; I've attached the standard SOC2 pack we share under NDA. Private option: we can run a dedicated (customer-isolated) deployment for PoC if you prefer, but it requires a short setup window and a signed MSA/SOW. For the PoC we can also support VPC peering to keep traffic inside your network.

4) Cost model / credits
- We typically provide evaluation credits for PoC engagements and can cap spend for the first 30 days. I’ll work with finance to confirm an exact cap and include in the SOW.

Proposed immediate actions (Michael / Dev to handle)
- Michael: share adapter sample and brief benchmark PDF.
- Dev: confirm VPC peering steps and timeline for dedicated PoC (if chosen).
- Marissa: share SOW/proposal + tentative schedule (attached).

Attached: redwood-proposal-ACME-042.pdf (SOW + PoC timeline), redwood-technical-summary.pdf, benchmark-summary.pdf

Proposed kickoff times: Tue Mar 9 09:00-09:30 PST or Wed Mar 10 10:00-10:30 PST. What works best?

Thanks
Marissa Cole
